events.title: United 2026 Bid Formally Announced
events.detail: The United States Soccer Federation, Canada Soccer, and the Mexican Football Federation jointly announced the "United 2026" bid for the FIFA World Cup, marking the first tri-nation hosting proposal in the tournament's history. The bid positioned the joint hosting model as a logistical and commercial breakthrough.

events.title: FIFA Awards 2026 Hosting Rights to United Bid
events.detail: At the 68th FIFA Congress in Moscow, the joint USA/Canada/Mexico bid won the right to host the 2026 FIFA World Cup, defeating Morocco 134 votes to 65. The decision followed controversy over FIFA's anti-corruption framework and concerns about the Moroccan bid's readiness.

events.title: FIFA Confirms 48-Team Expanded Format
events.detail: The FIFA Council unanimously approved the expansion of the World Cup from 32 to 48 teams beginning with the 2026 edition. The new format introduces 12 groups of four teams, with the top two from each group plus the eight best third-place finishers advancing to a Round of 32. The change adds 40 matches and extends the tournament by 7 days.

events.title: FIFA Announces All 16 Official Host Cities
events.detail: FIFA officially confirmed all 16 host cities for the 2026 World Cup: 11 in the United States (Atlanta, Boston, Dallas, Houston, Kansas City, Los Angeles, Miami, New York/New Jersey, Philadelphia, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle), 3 in Mexico (Guadalajara, Mexico City, Monterrey), and 2 in Canada (Toronto, Vancouver). The announcement confirmed MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ as the Final venue.

events.title: Official Tournament Brand Identity Unveiled
events.detail: FIFA unveiled the official visual identity, emblem, and branding for the 2026 World Cup. The emblem features a stylized trophy design incorporating North American cultural elements representing all three host nations. The identity was revealed in a global ceremony broadcast from Los Angeles.

events.title: Official Match Schedule Framework Released
events.detail: FIFA released the framework match schedule for the 2026 World Cup, confirming tournament dates, venue rotation plans, and the structure of travel clusters. The US will host 78 of 104 matches; Mexico and Canada will each host 13. All quarterfinals, semifinals, and the Final will be played at US venues.

events.title: MetLife Stadium Confirmed as World Cup Final Venue
events.detail: FIFA officially confirmed MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — the New York Giants and Jets NFL home — as the venue for the 2026 World Cup Final on July 19, 2026. With a capacity of 82,500, it will be the largest venue used in a World Cup since Brazil's Maracanã in 2014. AT&T Stadium (Dallas) and Mercedes-Benz Stadium (Atlanta) were named semi-final venues.

events.title: SoFi Stadium (LA) Confirmed for US Opening Match
events.detail: SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California — the home of the LA Rams and Chargers — was confirmed as the venue for the United States' opening group stage match on June 12, 2026. The $5.5 billion stadium, opened in 2020, is also slated to host the Opening and Closing Ceremonies of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.

events.title: Estadio Azteca Set for World Cup Opening Match
events.detail: FIFA confirmed Estadio Azteca in Mexico City as the venue for the tournament's opening match on June 11, 2026 — giving Mexico the honor of kickstarting the first 48-team World Cup. The historic stadium, which previously hosted 1970 and 1986 World Cup finals, underwent renovations to meet modern FIFA standards and safety requirements.

events.title: CONCACAF League Qualifying Phase Begins
events.detail: The CONCACAF qualifying process for non-host nations kicked off with the league phase. CONCACAF allocated 6 berths for the region (beyond the automatic host spots for USA, Mexico, and Canada), with additional intercontinental playoff paths available. The expanded format created high stakes across the Caribbean and Central American nations.

events.title: Argentina Clinches CONMEBOL Top Spot with Record Points
events.detail: Defending World Cup champions Argentina topped the CONMEBOL qualifying table with a record 38 points, confirming their place at the 2026 tournament. Brazil, Colombia, Uruguay, Ecuador, and Paraguay also secured automatic qualification. Bolivia qualified for the intercontinental playoff as the seventh-place team.

events.title: AFC Sends 8 Teams: Japan, South Korea, Iran, Australia, Jordan, Uzbekistan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar
events.detail: Asia's qualifying process concluded with eight direct qualifiers: Japan, Iran, South Korea, Jordan, Australia, and Uzbekistan from the third round, plus Saudi Arabia and Qatar through the fourth round. Iraq advanced to the intercontinental playoff as Asia's remaining contender. All four major Asian football powers earned direct berths.

events.title: Scotland Qualifies for First World Cup Since 1998
events.detail: Scotland secured qualification for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, ending a 28-year absence from the tournament since France 1998. The achievement was celebrated as a watershed moment for Scottish football, capping a significant improvement under national team management and qualifying through the UEFA zone.

events.title: Nine African Nations Qualify: CAF Allocation Expanded
events.detail: Africa's expanded allocation of 9+1 spots was filled, with Algeria, Cape Verde, Egypt, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Morocco, Senegal, South Africa, and Tunisia qualifying directly. Cape Verde made history as a first-time qualifier. DR Congo earned an intercontinental playoff spot by winning a decisive CAF playoff tournament ahead of Nigeria, Gabon, and Cameroon.

events.title: Haiti, Panama, Curaçao Qualify; Curaçao Makes History
events.detail: CONCACAF's three direct qualifying spots (beyond the hosts) were claimed by Haiti, Panama, and Curaçao. Curaçao's qualification was historic — the island nation became the smallest country ever to qualify for a FIFA World Cup by population. Jamaica and Suriname advanced to the intercontinental playoff.

events.title: UEFA Direct Qualifiers Confirmed: England, France, Germany, Spain Lead 12-Team Bloc
events.detail: Twelve European nations secured direct World Cup qualification: England, France, Germany, Spain, Portugal, Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, Austria, Norway, Croatia, and Scotland. Four additional European berths remained to be decided by playoff matches in March 2026. Italy — notably — failed to qualify automatically and faced a playoff.

events.title: New Zealand Qualifies as OFC's Direct Representative
events.detail: New Zealand secured Oceania's direct World Cup berth, qualifying for their sixth World Cup. New Caledonia also advanced from OFC to participate in the intercontinental playoff, giving Oceania a chance for a second representative at the 2026 tournament.

events.title: USMNT 26-Man World Cup Roster Announced — Pulisic Captains; Reyna Returns; Luna and Tessmann Snubbed
events.detail: Mauricio Pochettino unveiled the United States' official 26-man World Cup squad at The Rooftop at Pier 17 in New York City on May 26, broadcast live on FOX. Christian Pulisic captains; Giovanni Reyna returns after fitness concerns; Alejandro Zendejas (Club América) is the headline surprise call-up. Diego Luna (Sporting CP) and Tanner Tessmann (Venezia) were controversially omitted. Average squad age: 26 years 332 days — the fifth youngest in US national team history. Squad includes Sergiño Dest, Folarin Balogun, Tim Ream, Patrick Mahomes-era Kansas City native Weston McKennie, and goalkeeper Matt Turner. Chris Richards (ankle ligaments) included despite injury concerns. USMNT Group D: vs Paraguay (June 12, SoFi Stadium LA), Kosovo (June 16, AT&T Stadium Dallas), Australia (June 21, NRG Stadium Houston).

media.caption: Pochettino announces USMNT 26-man World Cup roster at Pier 17, New York City on May 26 — Pulisic captains, Reyna returns

events.title: FIFA Officially Publishes All 48 World Cup Squads — 1,248-Player Tournament Field Locked In, 9 Days to Kickoff
events.detail: FIFA officially published the confirmed 26-man squad lists for all 48 nations on June 2 — one day after the June 1 submission deadline — freezing the complete 1,248-player field for the first 48-team World Cup. The publication confirms: Lionel Messi (Argentina) equals Cristiano Ronaldo's record of six World Cup appearances; Manuel Neuer (40) returns from international retirement for Germany; Portugal carries an honorary 27th place for the late Diogo Jota; Iran's squad (led by captain Mehdi Taremi) is included despite zero US visas being issued to any delegation member with 9 days to their June 15 Group G opener. England's FA simultaneously released squad numbers — Harry Kane #9, Jude Bellingham #10, Bukayo Saka #7. The June 2 publication marks the definitive pre-tournament freeze: no further additions permitted except FIFA-approved injury replacements.

media.caption: All 48 FIFA World Cup 2026 squad lists officially published on June 2 — 9 days to kickoff at Estadio Azteca

events.title: FIFA Relocates Final Draw from Las Vegas to Washington D.C.
events.detail: FIFA moved the Final Draw venue from Las Vegas (the originally planned location) to the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C., reportedly at the request of President Donald Trump. The change drew criticism from observers who argued it gave the US President an undue platform at a sporting event. FIFA officials cited the prestige of the Washington venue.

events.title: Final Draw Held at Kennedy Center — 12 Groups Revealed
events.detail: FIFA held the official Final Draw at the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C., with Presidents Trump, Sheinbaum, and Canadian PM Carney opening the first ballot. All 48 teams were drawn into 12 groups (A–L). Key matchups included Mexico vs. South Africa (Group A, opening match), USA vs. Paraguay and Australia (Group D), and England vs. Croatia (Group L). France (Group I) and Argentina (Group J) were drawn into opposite pathways.

events.title: FIFA Awards Trump Inaugural 'Peace Prize' at Draw Ceremony
events.detail: At the Final Draw, FIFA President Gianni Infantino presented Donald Trump with FIFA's inaugural 'Peace Prize,' described as recognition for his 'exceptional and extraordinary actions to promote peace and unity around the world.' The award was created without formal FIFA Council approval and drew immediate criticism from human rights organizations, journalists, and football governance experts who questioned FIFA's independence.

events.title: Full 104-Match Schedule Published
events.detail: One day after the Final Draw, FIFA released the complete 104-match schedule for all venues and dates. The opening match was confirmed as Mexico vs. South Africa at Estadio Azteca on June 11. The US opens June 12 at SoFi Stadium vs. Paraguay; Canada opens June 12 at BMO Field. The Final is set for MetLife Stadium on July 19, 2026.

events.title: Amnesty and HRW Issue Pre-Tournament Human Rights Warnings
events.detail: Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch published coordinated reports warning FIFA and host governments about human rights risks at the 2026 World Cup. Key concerns included US immigration enforcement near venues, LGBTQ+ safety in restrictive states, workers' rights under anti-union federal policies, and press freedom risks. Forty-six civil society organizations signed an open letter demanding action before kickoff.

events.title: Intercontinental Playoff Bracket Set: Guadalajara and Monterrey Host
events.detail: FIFA confirmed the intercontinental playoff bracket and venues for March 2026. Six teams — Jamaica, New Caledonia, Suriname, Bolivia, DR Congo, and Iraq — compete in two three-team mini-tournaments hosted in Guadalajara and Monterrey. The top two teams (one from each bracket) earn the final two World Cup berths. Semifinals play March 26 and finals March 31.

events.title: UEFA Playoff Paths Confirmed: Italy, Wales, Ukraine, Poland Among Contenders
events.detail: The four remaining European World Cup spots were set to be decided in March 2026 playoffs. Path A: Italy vs. Northern Ireland (semi), Wales vs. Bosnia-Herzegovina (semi), with the winners meeting in the final. Path B: Ukraine vs. Sweden (semi), Poland vs. Albania (semi). Italy — three-time World Cup champions — faced the prospect of a third consecutive playoff elimination.

events.title: Sport & Rights Alliance Issues Comprehensive Pre-Tournament Warning
events.detail: The Sport & Rights Alliance — comprising Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the ACLU, and Transparency International — published a comprehensive report warning that the 2026 World Cup faces an 'unprecedented convergence of human rights challenges.' The report detailed concerns over US anti-union federal policies exposing workers to exploitation, corruption risks in host nations, press freedom restrictions, and FIFA's inadequate enforcement of its own 2016 Human Rights Policy.

events.title: Intercontinental Playoff Semifinals: Bolivia Beat Suriname 2–1; Jamaica Beat New Caledonia 1–0
events.detail: The FIFA intercontinental playoff semifinals produced clear results on March 26, 2026. Bolivia defeated Suriname 2–1 at Estadio BBVA in Monterrey (Paniagua 72', Terceros pen 79') to advance to the Pathway 2 final vs Iraq on March 31. Jamaica defeated New Caledonia 1–0 at Estadio Akron in Guadalajara (Bailey Cadamarteri) to advance to the Pathway 1 final vs DR Congo. The two finals on March 31 determine the last two World Cup berths in the 48-team field.

events.title: UEFA Playoff Semifinals: Eight Nations Advance — Kosovo Stun Slovakia 4–3, Gyökeres Hat-trick for Sweden
events.detail: All eight UEFA World Cup playoff semifinals were played on March 26, producing dramatic results. Italy beat Northern Ireland 2–0 (Path A, Tonali + Kean). Bosnia-Herzegovina eliminated Wales on penalties after a 1–1 AET draw (Path A). Sweden thrashed Ukraine 3–0 via a Viktor Gyökeres hat-trick (Path B). Poland defeated Albania 2–1 (Path B). Turkey edged Romania 1–0 through Kadioglu 53' (Güler assist) (Path C). Kosovo stunned Slovakia 4–3 in the day's biggest upset (Path C). Denmark routed North Macedonia 4–0 (Path D). Czechia beat Republic of Ireland 4–2 on penalties after 2–2 AET (Path D). All four Path finals are set for March 31.

events.title: FIFA Opens Last-Minute Ticket Sales Phase from April 1
events.detail: FIFA announced on March 26 that a final last-minute ticket sales phase for the 2026 World Cup will begin April 1 on a first-come, first-served basis. Over one million tickets were sold in prior windows amid unprecedented demand — more than 500 million applications received. The announcement follows sustained fan and player backlash over pricing, with Final tickets reaching $143,750 on FIFA's official resale platform.

events.title: Iran Issues Formal Travel Ban to 'Hostile' Countries — World Cup Crisis Escalates
events.detail: Iran's Ministry of Sports issued a formal ban on March 27 prohibiting all Iranian national and club teams from traveling to countries classified as 'hostile,' stating: 'The presence of national and club teams in countries that are considered hostile and are unable to ensure the security of Iranian athletes and team members is prohibited until further notice.' While triggered by a club football scheduling dispute, the order directly blocks Iran's three World Cup Group G matches — all scheduled at US venues (Los Angeles and Seattle). Iran's ambassador in Mexico City was reported negotiating with FIFA to relocate matches to Mexico; FIFA again rejected the request. Iran's sports minister had declared in March that Iran 'under no circumstances' could participate in the US. Six Iranian women's national team players reportedly sought asylum in Australia earlier in March after refusing to sing the national anthem.

events.title: USMNT 2–5 Belgium — Pre-World Cup Alarm After Atlanta Rout
events.detail: The United States Men's National Team suffered a 2–5 defeat to Belgium (FIFA 9th) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta (att. 66,867). Belgium outshot the US 21–12. Weston McKennie opened the scoring (39', Antonee Robinson assist) but Belgium dominated after halftime through Debast, Onana, De Ketelaere (pen) and a Lukébakio brace. Agyemang pulled one back (87'). Coach Pochettino said the team failed to 'keep the intensity.' The USMNT debuted new 'Stars and Stripes' Nike kits. Portugal follow on March 31, the last match before the May 26 roster announcement.

events.title: Amnesty 'Humanity Must Win' Report: World Cup Risks 'Stage for Repression'
events.detail: Amnesty International published its major pre-tournament report warning the 2026 World Cup risks becoming a 'stage for repression.' The report cited a 'human rights emergency' in the US under the Trump administration — mass deportations, ICE enforcement near stadiums, LGBTQ+ rollbacks — and called on FIFA and all three host governments to take urgent protective action. With $11 billion at stake and 73 days to kickoff, FIFA has not secured any formal moratorium on immigration enforcement near venues.

events.title: Six World Cup Finals on March 31 — Full 48-Team Field Confirmed
events.detail: All remaining World Cup berths were decided on March 31 in six simultaneous finals. UEFA results: Bosnia-Herzegovina beat Italy on penalties (Group B); Sweden beat Poland 3–0 (Group F); Kosovo beat Turkey 4–1 (Group D — joins USA, Paraguay, Australia); Denmark beat Czechia (Group A). FIFA Intercontinental results: DR Congo beat Jamaica 1–0 AET via Axel Tuanzebe (Group K — Portugal, Colombia, Uzbekistan); Iraq beat Bolivia 2–1 (Group I — France, Senegal, Norway). Italy missed the World Cup for a third straight time. Kosovo qualified for their first-ever World Cup. DR Congo returned after 52 years. Iraq qualified despite extraordinary overland travel to Monterrey due to regional airspace closures.

events.title: USMNT 0–2 Portugal — Back-to-Back Losses Raise Pre-World Cup Alarm
events.detail: The USMNT lost 0–2 to Portugal at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta (att. 72,297). Goals from Francisco Trincão (37') and João Félix (59') exposed recurring defensive weaknesses. Portugal played without Ronaldo, Leão, and Diogo Costa. Combined with the 2–5 loss to Belgium on March 28, the US finished March camp 0–2 with a 2–7 aggregate — Pochettino's worst camp ahead of the home World Cup. The 26-man World Cup roster is due May 26; next friendly is May 31 vs Senegal in Charlotte.

events.title: FIFA Last-Minute Ticket Sales Open — Website Glitch Chaos on April 2
events.detail: FIFA's final ticket sales phase opened April 1 at 11:00 AM ET, first-come, first-served, amid sustained fan anger over pricing. On April 2, a technical error routed buyers into the wrong queue for 90+ minutes. US Congress members had formally written calling the tournament 'the most financially exclusionary ever.' The cheapest openly available final ticket starts at $2,790; the FIFA official resale platform reopened April 2 with secondary prices reaching $143,750.

events.title: FIFA Confirms Iran's World Cup Participation — Congress Decision April 30
events.detail: After attending Iran's 5–0 win over Costa Rica in Antalya on March 31, FIFA President Infantino publicly confirmed: 'Iran will be at the World Cup.' Iran's Football Federation VP affirmed FIFA compliance. But Iran's Sports Minister had declared Iran 'under no circumstances' can participate. The FIFA Congress in Vancouver on April 30 is the next decision point for contingency planning if the conflict continues. Iran's Group G matches remain at US venues: vs New Zealand (LA, June 15), vs Belgium (LA, June 21), vs Egypt (Seattle, June 26).

events.title: FSE & Euroconsumers File EU Commission Complaint Against FIFA Over Ticket Prices
events.detail: Football Supporters Europe (FSE) and Euroconsumers filed a formal complaint with the European Commission on April 3 alleging FIFA abused its dominant market position to impose excessive ticket prices for the 2026 World Cup. The complaint cites Final ticket face values reaching $10,990 (up from $8,680) with secondary prices hitting $143,750 — 41 times face value — on FIFA's own resale platform. The organizations called for an EU competition law investigation. The complaint follows a formal US Congress letter calling the tournament 'the most financially exclusionary ever' and the April 2 website glitch that left fans in the wrong queue for 90+ minutes. FIFA has not publicly responded.

events.title: USMNT Calls 27 Players for March Camp — Belgium and Portugal Friendlies Before World Cup
events.detail: US head coach Mauricio Pochettino named a 27-player squad for the March 2026 camp, with the USMNT playing Belgium (March 28) and Portugal (March 31) in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium — the final major test matches before the 26-player World Cup roster is announced. Notable returns include defender Antonee Robinson (back from injury after missing all of 2025 international duty) and Chris Richards (named 2025 US Soccer Male Player of the Year). The USMNT debuted new Stars and Stripes kits at these fixtures.

events.title: Iran Sports Minister: Participation 'Very Low' Without Security Guarantees — Relocation Request Still Valid
events.detail: Iran Sports Minister Ahmad Donyamali told Anadolu Agency on April 5 that Iran's relocation request 'is still valid, but we have not yet received a response.' He offered the government's first conditional opening: 'If the relevant security guarantees are provided, our government will decide on Iran's participation.' Bloomberg analysis on April 6 concluded that relocating Iran's matches is 'extraordinarily difficult' and without modern historical precedent, citing FIFA host city agreements, broadcast contracts, and ticket allocations all structured around fixed venues. FIFA President Infantino maintains 'there is no Plan B, C, or D.' The disconnect between Iran's football federation (willing to compete) and its government (opposing participation at US venues) remains unresolved 24 days before the April 30 FIFA Congress in Vancouver — the formal decision point.

events.title: Serge Gnabry Rules Himself Out of World Cup — Germany's Injury Crisis Deepens
events.detail: German forward Serge Gnabry confirmed via Instagram on April 22 that his World Cup dream is 'sadly over' after an adductor muscle tear in his right leg sustained during Bayern Munich training. Expected recovery is approximately three months — ruling him out of Germany's Group E campaign opener vs. Curaçao on June 14 at Estadio Azteca. Gnabry (30, 44 caps) was a key attacker under Julian Nagelsmann, who now faces a forward line dependent on Florian Wirtz, Jamal Musiala, and Kai Havertz. Germany's squad concerns are compounded by Leroy Sané's ongoing injury doubts. Group E: Germany vs. Curaçao (June 14, Mexico City), vs. Ivory Coast (June 18, Kansas City), vs. Ecuador (June 23, Boston).

events.title: Rubio Clears Iran Players for World Cup — But Bars IRGC-Linked Personnel; Taremi's Visa Under Scrutiny
events.detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on April 24 that Iran's players may attend the 2026 World Cup — 'Nothing from the US has told them they can't come' — but drew a hard line: anyone with ties to the IRGC (designated by Washington as a foreign terrorist organization) will be denied entry. 'They can't bring a bunch of IRGC terrorists into our country and pretend they are journalists and athletic trainers,' Rubio said. President Trump added his administration 'would not want to affect the athletes.' The statement raised urgent concern about Iran's squad: Iran captain Mehdi Taremi (Inter Milan) served at an IRGC Navy base in Bushehr 2010–2012; multiple other squad members also completed mandatory IRGC service. Iran's Football Federation president Mehdi Taj confirmed replacement players have been identified for those denied visas. The statement is the clearest direct US government position on Iran participation and came exactly 6 days before the FIFA Congress in Vancouver on April 30 — the formal decision point.

events.title: Iran FA Chief Taj Demands FIFA Guarantee IRGC Will Not Be Insulted — New Condition Before Zurich Meeting
events.detail: Iran Football Federation president Mehdi Taj issued a new political condition on May 6: FIFA must provide official guarantees that the United States will not insult the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). 'Our host is FIFA, not Mr. Trump or America,' Taj said. The demand follows Taj's own April 29 denial of entry to Canada due to alleged IRGC ties, causing him to miss the FIFA Congress. He confirmed a Zurich meeting with FIFA President Infantino later in May. The condition is near-impossible to satisfy: the US officially designates the IRGC as a Foreign Terrorist Organization. Iran's football federation separately posted World Cup kit photos on May 5, signaling the federation — if not the government — is preparing for the tournament. The provisional squad is due May 11 and the final 26-man roster due June 1.

events.title: FIFA Extends Prestianni Ban Globally — Argentina Winger Could Miss First Two World Cup Group Games
events.detail: FIFA's Disciplinary Committee ruled on May 6 that the six-game UEFA ban on Argentina winger Gianluca Prestianni (Benfica, 20) is extended to have worldwide effect, ruling him out of Argentina's first two World Cup group matches if selected. The ban stems from a February 17, 2026 Champions League match in which Prestianni admitted to using a homophobic slur against Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid. If included in Scaloni's final 26-man squad (due June 1), Prestianni would miss Group J openers vs. Algeria (June 17) and vs. Austria (June 21) at Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City, potentially returning for Jordan (June 25). Argentina's preliminary squad (35–55 players) is due to FIFA on May 11.

events.title: FIFA Sets May 20 Zurich Meeting with Iran — Taj Hints at Withdrawal as Deadline Clock Runs
events.detail: FIFA formally invited Iran Football Federation president Mehdi Taj to Zurich on May 20 for direct talks with FIFA President Gianni Infantino — the last formal diplomatic channel before the June 1 final squad deadline. Taj escalated on May 7, suggesting a 'different decision' on Iran's World Cup participation could follow if FIFA cannot guarantee Iranian players and staff will not face politically motivated questioning over IRGC links. The May 20 meeting falls 22 days before the June 11 tournament opener. Iran's preliminary squad list is due May 11 (4 days). Iran Group G matches remain at US venues: SoFi Stadium (June 15 vs New Zealand, June 21 vs Belgium), Lumen Field (June 26 vs Egypt).

events.title: Iran-FIFA Hold 'Positive' Istanbul Crisis Talks — Grafstrom Says No Visa Guarantees Confirmed; Zurich Summit 3 Days Away
events.detail: FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom met Iran Football Federation President Mehdi Taj in Istanbul on May 17 — a surprise pre-Zurich meeting conducted while Iran's squad was simultaneously assembling in Antalya, Turkey for a training camp. Both sides described the talks as 'excellent and constructive.' Taj said FIFA 'listened to Iran's 10 raised points and offered solutions for each of them.' Grafstrom said FIFA was 'looking very much forward to welcoming them to the World Cup.' However, Grafstrom declined to confirm explicit US visa guarantees — the central unresolved issue — when specifically questioned. Not one Iranian player or coaching staff member had received a US visa as of May 17. The formal FIFA-Infantino-Taj Zurich summit is May 20; Iran's June 1 squad deadline is 15 days away. Group G: SoFi LA (June 15 vs New Zealand; June 21 vs Belgium), Lumen Seattle (June 26 vs Egypt). 25 days to the June 11 opener at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: Iran-FIFA Istanbul crisis talks May 17 — Grafstrom and Taj describe discussions as 'positive' but no visa guarantees confirmed

events.title: 4 Days to Provisional Squad Deadline — France May 14, USA May 26; Messi Confirmed in Argentina Plans
events.detail: With the May 11 FIFA provisional squad submission deadline four days away, all 48 nations are finalizing their selections. France announces their 26-man squad May 14 (Mbappé expected; Ekitike confirmed out, Achilles). Brazil announces May 18 (Rodrygo out, ACL; Estevao in doubt, hamstring). Germany announces May 21. USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino will reveal the 26-player roster at The Rooftop at Pier 17 in New York City on May 26, airing on FOX. Messi is among 21 players Scaloni has confirmed in Argentina's plans — preliminary squad due May 11; final squad June 1. All 48 nations' final 26-man panels are due to FIFA by June 1.

events.title: Paraguay Stuns Germany, Morocco Downs Netherlands on Penalties in World Cup Round of 32
events.detail: The Round of 32 delivered two of the tournament's biggest shocks: Paraguay eliminated Germany 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw, with Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann calling a disallowed extra-time goal for Jonathan Tah "a joke" after VAR review. Morocco eliminated the Netherlands 3-2 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Brazil beat Japan 2-1 at NRG Stadium, Houston, while Canada edged South Africa 1-0 at SoFi Stadium to reach the Round of 16 in Canada's first-ever men's World Cup knockout match.

media.caption: World Cup bracket after Germany and Netherlands were eliminated on penalties in the Round of 32

events.title: Argentina, Egypt Advance in Dramatic Finishes as World Cup Round of 32 Concludes
events.detail: The Round of 32 wrapped up July 1-3: France beat Sweden 3-0 (Mbappe brace), Norway beat Cote d'Ivoire 2-1 on Erling Haaland's 86th-minute winner, Mexico beat Ecuador 2-0 at Estadio Azteca, England beat DR Congo 2-1, Belgium beat Senegal 3-2 after extra time, USA beat Bosnia & Herzegovina 2-0, Spain beat Austria 3-0, Portugal beat Croatia 2-1, Switzerland beat Algeria 2-0, Egypt beat Australia 4-2 on penalties, Colombia beat Ghana 1-0, and Argentina beat Cabo Verde 3-2 after extra time, with Lionel Messi scoring his 7th career World Cup goal. All 16 Round of 16 matchups are now set.

media.caption: Round of 32 concludes with Argentina and Egypt both advancing in extra time and on penalties

events.title: Argentina Edges Egypt 3-2, Switzerland Survives Colombia on Penalties as Round of 16 Wraps
events.detail: The Round of 16 concluded July 4-7: Morocco routed Canada 3-0, France beat Paraguay 1-0, Norway beat Brazil 2-1, England beat Mexico 3-2 at Estadio Azteca, Spain beat Portugal 1-0, and Belgium beat the United States 4-1 at Lumen Field, Seattle -- a match that drew a US-record 33.086 million viewers on Fox, the most-watched soccer telecast in American television history. Argentina beat Egypt 3-2, scoring three unanswered goals in a 13-minute span; Egypt's football association said it "cannot remain silent" over the officiating. Switzerland eliminated Colombia 4-3 on penalties after a scoreless draw. Quarterfinalists: Morocco, France, Norway, England, Spain, Belgium, Argentina, Switzerland.

media.caption: USA's Round of 16 exit to Belgium drew a US-record 33 million viewers on Fox

events.title: France, Spain, England, Argentina Reach Semifinals; Mbappe Injury Scare, FIFA Adjusts VAR Protocol
events.detail: Quarterfinals: France beat Morocco 2-0 (Jul 9) -- Kylian Mbappe left the pitch late with what he described as a "minor ankle injury," saying afterward he was "completely fine"; Spain beat Belgium 2-1 (Jul 10), the only goal Spain has conceded all tournament; England beat Norway 2-1 after extra time (Jul 11); Argentina beat Switzerland 3-1 after extra time (Jul 11). All four quarterfinals set US viewership records for the round, led by England-Norway's 21.8 million viewers on Fox. Following backlash over disputed knockout-stage calls, FIFA confirmed a change to its semifinal VAR protocol, stationing a lead and backup video match official on-site.

media.caption: World Cup quarterfinals set US TV ratings records across all four matches

events.title: Spain Beats France 2-0 in Dallas to Reach First World Cup Final Since 2010
events.detail: Mikel Oyarzabal converted a 22nd-minute penalty and Pedro Porro added a second in the 58th as Spain beat France 2-0 at Dallas Stadium in the tournament's first semifinal. Spain has now conceded only one goal across seven matches -- to Belgium in the quarterfinals -- the tournament's stingiest defensive run. It is Spain's first World Cup final appearance since winning the title in 2010.

media.caption: Spain beat France 2-0 in Dallas to reach the World Cup final

events.title: Argentina Rallies Past England 2-1 in Atlanta; First-Ever Spain vs Argentina Final Set
events.detail: Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 in Atlanta, with Lionel Messi again a driving factor in a late rally, sending Argentina into the World Cup final for the first time since 2022. England will instead play France in the third-place playoff. The final -- Spain vs Argentina, Sunday July 19 at MetLife Stadium, New Jersey -- is the first-ever World Cup final meeting between the two nations.

media.caption: Messi fuels Argentina's rally past England, setting up the first-ever Spain vs Argentina World Cup final

events.title: England Beats France 6-4 in Wild Third-Place Playoff
events.detail: Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick — including a stoppage-time penalty — as England beat France 6-4 at Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, England's best World Cup finish since 1966. Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa also scored as England built a 4-0 halftime lead before surviving a fightback led by Kylian Mbappé's second-half brace, which took Mbappé past Lionel Messi for the all-time World Cup scoring record (22 goals) and to 10 goals at the tournament. It was the highest-scoring World Cup match since 1982 and the most goals ever in a third-place playoff.

media.caption: Harry Kane and England teammates celebrate their 6-4 win over France

events.title: Spain Beats Argentina 1-0 in Extra Time to Win 2026 World Cup
events.detail: Substitute Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute as Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup — Spain's second title, first since 2010, in front of a sellout crowd of 80,663. Argentina failed to register a shot on target in 90 minutes of regulation; goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made a World Cup final record 11 saves to keep the score level into extra time. Rodri won the Golden Ball, Kylian Mbappé the Golden Boot (10 goals, his second straight), Unai Simón the Golden Glove, and Pau Cubarsí Best Young Player — Spain took three of the four major individual honors. It may have been Lionel Messi's final World Cup; he was seen in tears afterward, posting 'The pain is immense and it will take time for this wound to heal.'

media.caption: Ferran Torres celebrates his extra-time winner as Spain beats Argentina 1-0

events.title: Up to 2 Million Fans Greet Spain's Champions in Madrid
events.detail: An estimated 1.8-2 million supporters lined Madrid's streets as Spain's World Cup squad paraded to Cibeles Square, where roughly 120,000 gathered. King Felipe VI received the squad at Zarzuela Palace before players met PM Pedro Sánchez. Golden Ball winner Rodri displayed the trophy and his award on stage. The win makes Spain the first nation to hold the men's and women's World Cup titles simultaneously.

media.caption: Spain's squad on the open-top bus during the Madrid victory parade

events.title: Tournament Sets All-Time Attendance and US Viewership Records
events.detail: FIFA confirmed a record 6,810,966 fans attended the 104 matches — nearly double the 1994 record — at 99.7% occupancy. The Spain-Argentina final drew 38.937M viewers on Fox (a US soccer broadcast record) plus 22.6M on Telemundo, for 60M+ combined US viewers; FIFA put the tournament's global broadcast audience at roughly 1.8 billion, with tournament revenue exceeding $11B.

media.caption: A sold-out MetLife Stadium for the World Cup final

events.title: Conspiracy Theories Spread Online Over Spain's Final Win
events.detail: A week after the final, misleading claims circulated widely: a post viewed nearly 4 million times alleged Infantino struck a deal with UEFA to fix Spain's win in exchange for 2027 re-election support (no evidence; Argentina had zero shots on target); another claimed FIFA punished Argentina for the Falklands banner; a third misread Messi telling teammates to 'stay calm' as evidence of threats. Argentina's federation dismissed all three claims.

media.caption: Spain players celebrate their World Cup final win

events.title: FIFA Opens Formal Disciplinary Case Against Argentina Over Falklands Banner
events.detail: FIFA's Disciplinary Committee formally opened proceedings against the Argentine Football Association over the 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' banner Giovani Lo Celso, Lisandro Martínez, and Nicolás Otamendi displayed after Argentina's July 15 semifinal win over England — escalating the probe first announced July 16. The case also covers alleged discriminatory chants and a post-match altercation with Spanish players. Argentina President Javier Milei called the celebration 'perfectly valid.'

media.caption: Sky Sports coverage of FIFA's charges against Argentina

events.title: FIFA Scraps World Cup Stake-Sale Plan After European Boycott Threat
events.detail: Infantino abandoned a plan to sell a 20% stake in a new entity running FIFA competitions (targeting up to $4.2B at a $20B valuation) to Joshua Kushner's Thrive Eternal. UEFA and every major European federation threatened to boycott FIFA competitions, calling it a sale of the sport's 'soul.' Presidential adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned in protest and COO Kevin Lamour said staff were 'blindsided.' Infantino said the plan 'created divisions... no longer in the interest' of the game.

media.caption: FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who scrapped the stake-sale plan July 31

events.title: FIFA Leadership Crisis Deepens: Klaveness Calls for Resignation, Confederations Accuse Infantino of 'Deception'
events.detail: Fallout from the abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan escalated into a full leadership crisis for FIFA president Gianni Infantino. A crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco on August 5 produced an apology for 'mistakes' and a reaffirmation of internal backing, but critics were unmoved: Portuguese great Luís Figo said Infantino 'must go,' and on August 7 Norwegian FA president Lise Klaveness said 'there is no trust in Infantino now' and called for his resignation. FIFA accused unnamed parties of a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to undermine the president. The crisis peaked August 10 when UEFA, CONCACAF, and the AFC — representing three of FIFA's six confederations — issued a joint open letter accusing Infantino of a 'fundamental breach of trust' and 'deception,' calling the stake-sale episode a 'profound failure of judgment' and demanding an independent review. UEFA maintained its threatened boycott of FIFA competitions. President Trump publicly defended Infantino, whose bid for a fourth term faces a vote at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco on March 18, 2027.

media.caption: Gianni Infantino, facing calls to resign amid FIFA's World Cup stake-sale fallout

events.title: Federation Revolt Against Infantino Widens; FIFA Fires COO Kevin Lamour, FIFA VP Csányi Breaks Ranks
events.detail: The wave of national federations publicly withdrawing support for Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidential re-election grew through mid-to-late August: Ireland (Aug 13), New Zealand — the first Oceania federation to break ranks (Aug 14), Scotland (Aug 17), and Israel (Aug 18) all rescinded earlier endorsements, joining Wales, England, Germany, Denmark, Netherlands, Norway, Serbia, Finland, and Jordan. Six Arab federations (Qatar, Morocco, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon, Sudan) publicly reaffirmed support for Infantino on Aug 13, while CAF and CONMEBOL continued backing him, illustrating a geographic split ahead of the March 18, 2027 vote. On Aug 17, FIFA fired chief operating officer Kevin Lamour after he publicly accused Infantino of misleading staff over the abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan — Lamour had told the AP in late July he expected to lose his job for speaking out: "If that means I lose my job, then so be it... At least I'll sleep well tonight." The revolt reached FIFA's own leadership on Aug 19, when vice-president Sándor Csányi (Hungary) withdrew his backing, calling Lamour's firing the 'final straw' and becoming the most senior FIFA insider yet to break ranks; Montenegro and North Macedonia followed on Aug 20. Mexico remained CONCACAF's lone holdout in support of Infantino.

media.caption: Gianni Infantino, facing a widening wave of federation withdrawals — including FIFA vice-president Sándor Csányi on Aug 19 — and the firing of FIFA COO Kevin Lamour in mid-August

events.title: FIFA Bans Three Argentina Players Over World Cup Final Scuffle With Spain
events.detail: FIFA's Disciplinary Committee resolved its July 29 case over the post-final altercation between Argentina and Spain players: Leandro Paredes was banned 10 matches and fined $90,000 for grabbing Spain's Eric García by the throat and shoving Gavi, Nahuel Molina was banned seven matches and fined $90,000, Thiago Almada received a one-match ban and $30,000 fine, and assistant coach Roberto Ayala was banned three matches and fined $30,000. Spain's Gavi was handed a one-match ban and $30,000 fine. The Argentine Football Association was fined $321,000 combined and ordered to play its next two home matches at 50% stadium capacity. The ruling is separate from FIFA's still-open case against Argentina over the 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' banner from the July 15 semifinal.

media.caption: Leandro Paredes clashes with Spain players after the World Cup final — FIFA banned him 10 matches on Aug 21

events.title: Infantino Defies Caribbean Visit Request as Nordic Federations Revolt and Čeferin Rules Out FIFA Bid
events.detail: The FIFA leadership crisis widened over the weekend. Infantino defied a CONCACAF request from Victor Montagliani and attended a Caribbean Football Union youth event in Punta Cana, Dominican Republic (Aug 22), a visit read as lobbying Caribbean federations for re-election votes to split the Concacaf bloc. All six Nordic federations — Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and the Faroe Islands — issued a joint statement (Aug 23) declaring they had 'lost confidence' in Infantino and demanding binding guarantees against future private ownership of FIFA competitions plus an independent investigation into the abandoned stake-sale plan. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin then ruled himself out of challenging Infantino directly (Aug 24), saying 'my credibility is much, much, much higher if I'm not interested in the position,' but predicted Infantino will either step down or 'have a candidate against him' at the March 2027 vote — naming AFC president Sheikh Salman and Montagliani as possible challengers.

media.caption: UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin, who ruled out a FIFA presidency bid on Aug 24 while warning Infantino he faces a contested March 2027 election

events.title: Election Mechanics Come Into Focus as European Leagues Chief Says Infantino 'Has No Future' at FIFA
events.detail: The crisis moved from open letters to procedural mechanics. Coverage on Aug 25 detailed the path to unseating Infantino: he argues his 2016 partial term (completing Sepp Blatter's interrupted mandate) shouldn't count toward FIFA's three-term limit, a reading the FIFA Council backed in Dec 2022, but advocacy group FairSquare has formally asked FIFA's governance committee to rule him ineligible on those grounds. Any rival must secure 5 federation nominations by the Nov 18, 2026 deadline ahead of the March 18, 2027 vote in Rabat, where 106 of 211 votes decide the outcome; Victor Montagliani, Sheikh Salman, and Nasser Al-Khelaifi (who has denied interest) remain the most-discussed names, while CAF, CONMEBOL, Mexico, and Argentina continue backing Infantino. On Aug 26, Claudius Schaefer — president of European Leagues, representing 53 professional leagues — told The Athletic that Infantino 'cannot have a future' at FIFA, citing the unconsulted FIFA Peace Prize awarded to President Trump and the Trump-prompted reversal of USMNT forward Folarin Balogun's World Cup suspension as 'a real scandal' of political interference in sporting integrity, though he said reforming the presidency's powers matters more than replacing Infantino personally.

media.caption: Claudius Schaefer (European Leagues) and Gianni Infantino — Schaefer said Aug 26 that Infantino 'has no future' at FIFA

events.title: Italy Withdraws Support as UEFA Prepares Criminal Complaint Against Infantino
events.detail: The FIFA leadership crisis crossed from political pressure into formal legal jeopardy. The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) announced Aug 26 it was withdrawing support for Infantino's re-election, with president Giovanni Malagò citing 'the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning governance and the development of international competitions' and pledging to work with UEFA on 'a vision of football based on merit, solidarity, sustainability and the central role of fans' — making Italy the latest major European federation, after England, Germany, and the Netherlands, to break with him. The next day, court filings in Manhattan and southern Florida revealed UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code ('criminal mismanagement'), seeking discovery from two Florida-based FIFA entities — FIFA (AMERICAS), Inc. and FWC2026 US, Inc. UEFA's lawyers characterized the abandoned $4.2 billion World Cup stake-sale plan as using a price that was 'fraudulently off-market' and 'promoted by Infantino for his own benefit,' saying it was never competitively auctioned or independently valued. UEFA said it is suspending its own boycott threat 'on a provisional basis' while the legal process proceeds.

media.caption: Gianni Infantino, whose abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan is now the subject of a planned UEFA criminal complaint in Switzerland
